THE WILD TABLE OF LOVE
BY ARTISTS, GILLIE AND MARC
#Love TheLast #WildTableOfLove
The Wild Table of Love by internationally renowned artists, Gillie and Marc, features a
banquet table full of delicious food, hosted by internationally beloved hybrid characters,
Rabbitwoman and Dogman. Sharing their table with ten of the most endangered animals in
the world, they are opening their hearts to the wild world, promising to protect them from the
threat of extinction. When we sit and share a meal, we share friendship and support. With two
empty seats at the table, you can join the family of love, becoming a protector of wildlife and
saving many species from the threat of extinction. This is part of the broader 'Love The Last'
project, a social movement driven by public art to raise awareness, funds and support for
endangered animals across the world, encouraging people to take action before we lose these
animals forever.
The Wild Table of Love serves as a beacon for a brighter future.
Help share their story through the hashtags

Reculver Towers, Herne Bay

In 2014, six artists were commissioned to design and create a durable, unique and imaginative bench that celebrates an aspect or characteristic of Herne Bay for everyone. The six benches form a nice trail from Hampton to Reculver to
encourage visitors to explore the three miles of coastline of the Herne Bay Coastal Park.

This was Jason Onion's interpretation:

This bench is in memory of a family friend, story teller and bird enthusiast, Bert Addley of Herne Bay. It is also dedicated to the many customers, couples and friends - including Bert - who enjoyed the original Macaris Ice Cream parlour 1931 to 2008.

It was designed and created by Jason Charles Onion, an original member of the Macari family. The bench is made from reclaimed hardwood that was once part of the original Victorian sea defences.

Flora Calcarea chalk and Channel Way
Flora Calcarea is a collection of artworks created by the
artist Rob Kesseler for the Chalk and Channel Way between
Dover and Folkestone, which invites you to take a closer
look at the landscape and the rich botanical diversity
around us. The inspiration for this work was the thousands
of pressed dried plants in the herbarium at Kew Gardens.
The artist presents us with a fossilised book of dried flowers
from which the pages have escaped, blown along the path,
accompanied by highly magnified pollen specimens
collected from local flowers and photographed on a
scanning electron microscope at Kew.

The Chalk & Channel Way is part of
the National Cycle Network, route 2,
and artworks along the path have
been commissioned by a partnership
of Sustrans, the Countryside Agency
White Cliffs Countryside Project,
Kent Downs AONB, Eurotunnel
Arts Council England SE, Arts and
Business, Dover District Council and
Shepway District Council.
